question: which open-source engine should rank paraphrase queries over the real string bank?
population: strings/generated_candidates.jsonl — 170 records (the full bank, no sampling)
query_construction: hand-written paraphrases with minimal shared vocabulary; accept-sets resolved by substring audit of the bank BEFORE any engine ran
findings: learned LOCAL embeddings roughly double lexical/hash on paraphrase queries (MRR 0.55 vs 0.27-0.31) — three independent learned models converge, so the effect is real

AMONG learned models nothing separates at n=10: the 30MB static model ties the retrieval-tuned 32M and a full transformer on THIS bank — the smallest stays default per least-cost; NOT a verdict that bigger models never pay (no-premature-judgment rule: re-run at 10x bank size)

naive RRF fusion with a WEAK lexical leg degrades the strong vector leg (0.325 < 0.511) — hybrid is not automatically better than its best member (same lesson as the stacking-zoo ensemble evidence record)
hash_vector used the salted builtin hash() and silently violated the identical-ranking invariant across processes — caught by the semantic canary flapping between runs; fixed with crc32 bucketing

adopted.opt_in_vector: model2vec potion-base-8M via the 'rag' extra; model configurable (vector_model=)

verified_available_lanes.sqlite-vec v0.1.9: loads locally — the persistent single-file FTS5+vector store lane (wiring pending)
verified_available_lanes.nomic-embed-text via local ollama daemon: embeddings-are-LOCAL lawful; one backend flag away
verified_available_lanes.CodeRankEmbed 137M: code-specialized candidate for Code Node retrieval; needs sentence-transformers atop the present cpu torch (unmeasured here)

limits: n=10 queries over 170 records is a PILOT — engine ordering among learned models is NOT established; the frozen-query harness is the durable artifact and re-runs as the bank grows
recompute: the tournament script in this evidence record's session scratchpad; rebuild via strings/generated_candidates.jsonl + the probes list herein

round_2_20260824.question: is there an easy good ready-made implementation of the intelligence search? (owner question)

lancedb_vector_model2vec.note: identical to our vector leg — same embeddings, sanity check passes

findings: LanceDB IS the easy good implementation of the multi-channel core: one embedded library, no server, ~10 lines for FTS+vector+hybrid, sub-second indexing at this scale
its tantivy BM25 BEAT our FTS5 OR-match lexical (0.467 vs 0.308) — adopted as lexical_backend='lancedb' (the 'search' extra)
its native score-aware hybrid held at 0.533 where our naive RRF degraded to 0.325 — proper fusion resists a weak leg; adopting its hybrid as a Retriever mode is the queued follow-up
bm25s matched our FTS5 (0.268 vs 0.308) — no gain, not adopted
the full portfolio (typed contracts, structural code search, compiler/test gates) remains OURS — no library ships it, and the research itself warns frameworks would duplicate our ontology
round_2_20260824.limits: same 10-query/170-record pilot as round 1 — ordering among close engines is directional
